sec:elaboration-intro: The remaining sections elaborate the categorical, algebraic, and analytic context of the QOU axioms. They establish the TQFT setting, record the q-jacobiator identity, give the physical reading of the categorical action, and assemble the categorical lifting for the brane tower.
rem:tqft-context:
Remark TQFT context. The axioms of the quantum universe and quantum observable universe are modelled on the algebraic data of topological quantum field theory. The Frobenius--Hopf object A carries the 2d cobordism data and the Hopf structure for quantum-group symmetry. The precise form of the 2d-cobordism claim is the canonical isomorphism \mathbf{Cob}(2) \cong \mathbf{Cob}(3)_{S^2,\mathrm{CF}} [li2026-two-sphere] (Thm.~1.0.8): the commutative-Frobenius part of the S^2-sector of the oriented 3d bordism category is the 2d cobordism category, so Z(S^2) is a commutative Frobenius monoid for every 3d TFT Z, and its Frobenius structure is exactly the 2d cobordism data. The sector's remaining generators, one unit per closed oriented irreducible prime 3-manifold (Thm.~1.0.5), are not used by these axioms. The identification is at the level of the Frobenius structure only: Li's monoids are commutative in a symmetric monoidal target, whereas A is a Hopf algebra in a braided category and is not assumed commutative, and nothing here identifies A with Z(S^2) of a 3d TFT or bears on the Hopf half of the Frobenius--Hopf object.

The condition \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 acts as the categorical contact condition. It is the condition that would ensure irreducibility of an associated 3d TQFT; no such TQFT is constructed here, and at generic q > 1 the representation category has infinitely many simple objects, so it is not modular (unlike the compact-Lie-group extended 3d TQFTs classified by Daniel S. Freed, Michael J. Hopkins, Jacob Lurie, and Constantin Teleman [freed2010]). Within the framework it ensures non-degeneracy of the pairing across cobordisms, and full dualisability. In the archimedean realisation, this enforces H^0(M, \mathrm{Ad}(P)) = 0, eliminating infinitesimal automorphisms on the instanton connection.
sec:vanishing-explication:
Vanishing conditions.

In the archimedean \mathbb{C}-QOU, H^0(M, \mathrm{Ad}(P)) = 0 eliminates infinitesimal gauge symmetries, and \Gamma_c(M,\mathcal{S}) = 0 secures the injectivity of the jet-bundle map \Gamma(J^1 \mathcal{S}) \hookrightarrow \mathcal{A}(P).
rem:levi-generalisation:
Remark Generalisation beyond strict pseudoconvexity. The QOU framework relies on Levi non-degeneracy over strict pseudoconvexity, requiring three conditions:

  1. Kohn--Rossi finite-dimensionality: The tangential CR complex has finite-dimensional cohomology, securing analytic control over q-harmonic forms.
  2. Non-degeneracy of the aether: The Levi form L_\varTheta is non-degenerate, fixing the aether parameter q(p) = 1 + \lvert\langle L_\varTheta, F_A^+\rangle\rvert \geq 1.
  3. QOU vanishing: H^0(M, \mathrm{Ad}(P)) = 0 and \Gamma_c(M,\mathcal{S}) = 0 provide the topological gauge obstructions.
rem:quantum-gauge-group-category: Remark Quantum gauge group: category-theoretic perspective. The quantum gauge group operates fibrewise via the representation category \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_{q(p)}(2)). Tannaka--Krein duality reconstructs the Hopf algebra \mathcal{O}_{q(p)}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) through the forgetful fibre functor. The Hopf-algebra and representation-category viewpoints are equivalent across fibres.
rem:hopf-structure-diagrams: Remark Hopf-algebra structure: coassociativity. The Hopf comultiplication \Delta_q on \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) obeys coassociativity. This property is required for consistency across the theoretical framework.
def:quantum-flatness: Definition Quantum flatness (F_\nabla = B). Let B \in \Omega^2(A) \otimes \mathrm{Ad}(A) be the 2-form datum of the inner-automorphism 2-group \mathrm{INN}(G_q). The connection \nabla is quantum flat when its curvature equals the 2-form datum: F_\nabla = B.
rem:self-dual-2group: Remark Self-duality as constrained 2-group gauge theory. A 2-connection for \mathrm{INN}(G) dictates F_A = B. Under the simplicity constraint B \in \Gamma(\Lambda^+\!H^* \otimes \mathrm{Ad}(P)), the 2-form datum is self-dual. The conjunction of quantum flatness F_A = B and simplicity forces F_A = F_A^+, securing the instanton equation F_A^- = 0.
prop:emergence-to-quantum-flat: Proposition From Tannakian emergence to 2-group quantum flatness. For a QOU meeting the categorical volume constraint, G_q \cong \mathrm{SU}_q(2). The inner-automorphism strict 2-group \mathrm{INN}(G_q) of John C. Baez and Aaron D. Lauda [baez2004], corresponding to the identity crossed module \partial = \mathrm{id}_{G_q}, carries the vanishing fake-curvature condition F_A = B of John C. Baez and Urs Schreiber [baez-schreiber2007, §4], reproducing the instanton equation F_A^- = 0 under simplicity. Quantum flatness operates as a derived consequence of the instanton axiom.
prf:emergence-to-quantum-flat:
Proof Proof of From Tannakian emergence to 2-group quantum flatness. The argument proceeds in three steps.

Step 1: The volume constraint determines the Lie algebra. The categorical volume constraint provides a non-degenerate epimorphism \epsilon \colon \Lambda^2 V \to \mathbf{1}. Under the forgetful functor \tau, this endows the rank-2 module \tau(V) with a q-antisymmetric pairing whose invariance algebra is \mathfrak{su}_q(2). This is the Lie algebra of the reconstructed group G_q, and hence of the identity crossed module \partial \colon G_q \xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}} G_q defining the strict inner-automorphism 2-group \mathrm{INN}(G_q) under the crossed-module classification of John C. Baez and Aaron D. Lauda [baez2004].

Step 2: The determinant-one condition descends to the 2-form datum. For a general crossed module \partial \colon H \to G_q, vanishing fake curvature [baez-schreiber2007, §4] imposes F_A = \mathrm{d}\partial(B); for \mathrm{INN}(G_q) (\partial = \mathrm{id}_{G_q}), a 2-connection (A, B) takes values in \mathfrak{g}_q = \mathfrak{su}_q(2) and quantum flatness sets B = F_A directly, so B inherits the tracelessness forced by the determinant constraint \det(g_V) = 1 of \mathrm{SU}(2) emergence: B is \mathrm{Ad}(P)-valued with \mathrm{tr}B = 0, i.e. \mathfrak{su}_q(2)-valued rather than \mathfrak{gl}_q(2)-valued.

Step 3: Simplicity plus quantum flatness gives the instanton equation. Imposing the simplicity constraint B \in \Gamma(\Lambda^+\!H^* \otimes \mathrm{Ad}(P)) (self-dual 2-group) and combining with F_A = B yields F_A = F_A^+, hence F_A^- = 0. Infinitesimally, the equivalence between vanishing fake curvature and F_A^- = 0 under simplicity holds for any crossed module whose Lie-algebra differential \mathrm{d}\partial \colon \mathfrak{h} \to \mathfrak{g}_q is an isomorphism; selecting \mathrm{INN}(G_q) uniquely among strict 2-groups over G_q requires in addition group-level faithfulness \ker(\partial) = 1 and surjectivity \mathrm{coker}(\partial) = 1 so no discrete central kernel or outer quotient remains. Step 1 guarantees the structure group is \mathrm{SU}_q(2)---not a quotient of \mathrm{GL}_q(2)---so the instanton moduli space carries the gauge symmetry dictated by the categorical axioms.
rem:simplicity-from-category: Remark Categorical origin of the simplicity constraint. The *-involution enforces self-duality on the 2-forms. The categorical axioms mandate the sequence: volume constraint \Rightarrow G_q = \mathrm{SU}_q(2) \Rightarrow F_A = B \Rightarrow B = F_A^+ \Rightarrow F_A^- = 0. The geometric input reduces entirely to the CR structure.
rem:frobenius-simplification: Remark Frobenius structure of the C gauge algebra. The Haar state h_q induces a non-degenerate Frobenius pairing on \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)). The non-degeneracy of the Frobenius form forces H^0(M, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0, as any global parallel section in the adjoint representation would pair with itself against the irreducibility constraint.
rem:j1e-local-states: Remark J^1E as the space of local states. The jet bundle J^1 \mathcal{S} accommodates the local states. The aether parameter q weights the classical gauge dynamics on the instanton connection to constitute the quantum field algebra \mathrm{SU}_q(2).
sec:dq-squared-elaboration-intro: This section specialises the d_q^2 obstruction and the q-Lie bracket Jacobiator to a concrete manifold M. At q = 1, all deformed operators recover their classical counterparts.
prop:dq-squared: Proposition d_q^2 does not vanish. The archimedean specialisation yields d_q^2\alpha = q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})d\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha. Here d\varTheta operates as the symplectic form on H. d_q^2 = 0 if and only if q = 1 or \alpha is Reeb-invariant.
prf:dq-squared:
Proof Proof of d_q^2 does not vanish. Write a = q^{-1} and b = 1 - q^{-1}, so a + b = 1. Then

\begin{align*}
  d_q^2\alpha
  &= d_q\bigl(ad\alpha + b\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha\bigr) \\
  &= a^2d^2\alpha
     + abd(\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha)
     + ab\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_{\xi}d\alpha
     + b^2\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi(\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha).
\end{align*}

The first term vanishes since d^2 = 0. The second expands as abd\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha - ab\varTheta \wedge d\mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha. The third term cancels the second's negative part because [d, \mathcal{L}_\xi] = 0 implies \varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_{\xi}d\alpha = \varTheta \wedge d\mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha. For the fourth term, the Reeb field satisfies \mathcal{L}_\xi\varTheta = 0 (since \iota_\xi d\varTheta = 0 and \varTheta(\xi)=1), so \mathcal{L}_\xi(\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha) = \varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi^2\alpha; the factor \varTheta \wedge \varTheta = 0 in b^2\varTheta \wedge \varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi^2\alpha kills this term. Hence d_q^2\alpha = abd\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha.
prop:q-jacobiator:
Proposition Jacobiator of the q-Lie bracket. The archimedean specialisation violates the Jacobi identity for horizontal vector fields when q \neq 1. The Jacobiator reads

  \mathrm{Jac}_q(U,V,W) = -q^{-1}(1-q^{-1})\!\sum_{\mathrm{cyc}} d\varTheta(V,W)\mathcal{L}_\xi U.

Since the Levi form d\varTheta|_{H \times H} is non-degenerate, (\mathfrak{X}(M), [\cdot,\cdot]_q) forms a Leibniz algebra.
prf:q-jacobiator:
Proof Proof of Jacobiator of the q-Lie bracket. For horizontal V, W, the bracket reduces to [V,W]_q = q^{-1}[V,W]. The mixed term \varTheta([V,W]_q) = -q^{-1}d\varTheta(V,W) is in general non-zero. Substituting into the next bracket:

\begin{align*}
  [[V,W]_q, U]_q
  &= q^{-2}[[V,W],U]
    - q^{-1}(1-q^{-1})d\varTheta(V,W)\mathcal{L}_\xi U,
\end{align*}

using \varTheta(U)=0 and \varTheta([V,W]_q) = -q^{-1}d\varTheta(V,W). Summing cyclically, the q^{-2} terms assemble into q^{-2}\mathrm{Jac}(U,V,W) = 0 by the classical Jacobi identity, leaving only the d\varTheta terms.
rem:classical-recovery: Remark Classical recovery of q-deformed operators. At q = 1, the deformed operators recover their classical forms: d_1 = d, [\cdot,\cdot]_1 = [\cdot,\cdot], A_1 = A, and \xi_1 = \xi.
sec:physical-elaborations-intro: The deformed operators carry direct physical readings. This section extracts the q-torsion leaves, the properties of q-harmonic forms, the linearisation conventions, and the Schrödinger equation on the jet coaction.
rem:q-torsion-leaf-minimum: Remark q-Torsion leaves as energy minima. A q-torsion leaf L is a local minimum, on the horizontal distribution, of the curvature norm \lVert\nabla_q^2\rVert of the q-deformed connection \nabla_q. The Reeb-flow invariance forces the first variation of \lVert\nabla_q^2|_L\rVert to vanish, situating L inside a q-curvature well.
rem:q-harmonic-physical: Remark Physical interpretation of q-harmonicity. A q-harmonic form interpolates between classical Hodge harmonicity and the deep-quantum regime via the q-Laplacian \Delta_q. The harmonicity condition depends strictly on q.
sec:linearisation-convention:
Linearisation convention and the role of J.

The symbol i evaluates as the CR complex structure J \colon H \to H on the Levi distribution. The state bundle \mathcal{S} is linearised at a base section via stereographic projection, allowing the covariant derivative D_A to operate on \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{lin}}.
rem:schrodinger-jet-coaction:
Remark q-Deformed Schrodinger equation. For a section \psi \in \Gamma(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{lin}}), the Schrödinger dynamics dictate

  J\hbar_q(p)\iota_{\xi_q} D_A \psi =  \hat{H}_q \psi,

where \hat{H}_q = -\tfrac{1}{2}\hbar_q\Delta_q + V_q is the q-deformed Hamiltonian. The local quantum Planck constant is \hbar_q(p) = 1 - q(p)^{-1}. Contracting D_A\psi with the Reeb vector field \xi_q produces a section of \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{lin}}. As q(p) \to 1, uncertainty vanishes and the wave trajectory freezes classically.
prose:outro-quantum-observable-universes:
Chapter close — Quantum Observable Universes.

The Quantum Observable Universe chapter concludes. The aether parameter q controls the differentials, the Reeb derivation \xi guides the gauge group \mathrm{SU}_q(2), and the q-special functions provide the spectral pairing. The next two chapters survey concrete realisations across the five-step arc (Models of QOUs) and construct the recursive brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} (Lifting and Descent).
sec:five-step-arc-intro:
Every quantum observable universe passes through five structural stages that carry the abstract axioms of a braided monoidal category into numerical predictions for physical spectra. Each chapter of this monograph resides at a specific stage of this pipeline:

  1. Categorical stage. A rigid braided monoidal category (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) equipped with a Frobenius–Hopf object A, a fibre functor \tau, and an internal Reeb derivation \xi deformed by the aether parameter q.
  2. Algebraic stage. The representation of the n-strand braid group B_n on A^{\otimes n}, its factorization through the Iwahori–Hecke quotient H_n(q) generated by (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0, and its closure under the Jones–Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M.
  3. Geometric stage. The realization of closed braids as hyperbolic link complements embedded in the genus-four Bring surface \Sigma_4 (\chi(\Sigma_4) = -6, b_1(\Sigma_4) = 8, \mathrm{Area}(\Sigma_4) = 12\pi), where ideal q-tetrahedral volume and cohomological defect determine topological mass and three-colour charge.
  4. Archimedean stage. The ring extension R \to R[i] \to R[i][q, q^{-1}] evaluated at the aether parameter q_0, pairing the algebraic trace with hyperbolic period integrals via the non-abelian Stokes mass identity.
  5. Physical stage. The resulting dimensionless mass ratios, nuclear binding energies, \beta-decay Q-values, and electromagnetic and weak couplings, tested against experimental observation and extended to molecular braids.

This chapter defines the vocabulary of the five-step pipeline and surveys the concrete models—Archimedean contact manifolds, Calabi–Yau and ALE spaces, p-adic quantum groups, and finite-field fusion categories—that satisfy the axioms across distinct arithmetic regimes.
sec:step-categorical: Categorical step. The aether parameter q requires a structure to deform. At q = 1, the classical symmetric tensor category appears. For q \neq 1, the action resolves into a braided one. The aether is a rigid braided monoidal category (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) equipped with a Frobenius–Hopf object A and a fibre functor \tau. The parameter q records the deformation of this categorical action. The Reeb derivation \delta_q promotes q to a connection on the categorical bundle; its curvature is the Yekutieli MI tower. The axioms are developed, and the Reeb derivation derived, in subsequent chapters. Descent, jets, and the Gröbner–Shirshov filtration are developed to provide the categorical infrastructure.
sec:step-algebraic: Algebraic step. To turn the categorical action into a computable knot invariant, the construction passes from braids to a trace-carrying quotient. The braid group B_n acts on A^{\otimes n}. The quotient by the Hecke relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 is the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(q). This algebra controls the combinatorics of the categorical action. The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M packages braid words into a class function. Evaluation on \beta_K yields the Jones polynomial J_K(q) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_K)). This step develops braids, knot groups, the Hecke algebra, and the Skein-relation translation.
sec:step-geometric:
Bring's surface — the canonical geometric object. The geometric step realises the mass of every knot on one fixed surface. The canonical geometric realisation is Bring's surface \Sigma_4. This is the genus-4 smooth projective curve with Euler characteristic \chi = -6 and automorphism group \mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma_4) \cong S_5. It is the vanishing locus on \mathbb{P}^4 of the first three power sums:

  \Sigma_4 = \mathrm{Proj}\!\left(
    R[x_0,\dots,x_4]\Big/\bigl(\textstyle\sum x_j,
    \textstyle\sum x_j^2, \textstyle\sum x_j^3\bigr)
  \right).

Structural facts include:

  • \Sigma_4 has genus g = 4 and Euler characteristic \chi(\Sigma_4) = 2 - 2g = -6.
  • The automorphism group is \mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma_4) \cong S_5. The orientation-preserving subgroup A_5 \subset S_5 acts faithfully and supplies the symmetry group of the canonical particle assignment.
  • \Sigma_4 is the canonical archimedean model. The aether parameter q_0 is fixed by its \chi = -6 structure. The Reeb derivation produces a q-hyperbolic structure on \Sigma_4 with five S_5-equivalent fibres.
  • The cohomological defect of \Sigma_4 — the discrepancy between its first Betti number and the rank of the natural three-colour bundle — supplies the origin of the three-colour SU(3) charge of QCD.

Geometric step. The Reeb derivation lifts a braid word \beta_K to a Reeb flow. The complement S^3 \setminus K is a q-hyperbolic 3-manifold. By a theorem of Yekutieli, this complement carries a tessellation by ideal q-tetrahedra indexed by k = 0, 1, 2, 3 with cell coefficients (1, 4, 16, 64). The volume \mathrm{Vol}(K) of the complement is the central geometric invariant. This volume realises the topological mass of the knot. Evaluating it on \Sigma_4 assigns each knot its mass. The cohomological defect of \Sigma_4 supplies the three-colour charge. The surface fixes both the mass and the colour structure. This step derives the volume identity, the tangle-energy decomposition, and the mass-endomorphism statement.
sec:step-archimedean:
Archimedean step. Specialisation at the observed aether parameter q_0 produces archimedean (real-valued, dimensional) quantities and yields a dimensional mass. The machinery is a chain of extensions of the generic categorical content. Stated over a commutative ring R, it specialises through R \to R[i] \to R[i][q, q^{-1}]. The parameter q is uniquely extracted as a categorical invariant (uniqueness of the aether parameter); its value q_0 at the location and energy scale of observation is observed, not derived from Bring topology.

The mass endomorphism \mathfrak{m}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K) \cdot c_q^{-2} is the non-abelian Stokes integration of the Reeb flow against the categorical action. It is evaluated using Wedderburn decomposition, partition channels y_\lambda \chi^\lambda, crystal bases, and \Delta_\lambda gating.

Alternatives to the archimedean specialisation include p-adic (R \to \mathbb{Q}_p) and characteristic-p (R \to \mathbb{F}_p[T]) aether completions. These are non-archimedean and do not produce dimensional masses.
sec:step-physical:
Physical step. The archimedean specialisation at the aether parameter q_0 on Bring's surface computes a particle spectrum from the three calibration inputs: the electron mass m_e (fixing the mass scale), the weak-channel aether modulus q_0 (ideal proxy m_\mu/m_e; pinned numerically on m_{\mathfrak{p}}/m_e, which leaves m_\mu/m_e as a model comparison; which pin the numbers use), and the pion mass m_\pi (fixing the orthogonal meson class). This step develops the particle-generation mechanism (LP/SDP confinement, operator-valued folding/unfolding). It derives Pauli exclusion and the T(2,n) fermion/boson split from the rigid-braided structure. It catalogues these model evaluations (leptons, quarks, baryons, nuclei, \mathfrak{Q}_\beta, magnetic moments) and compares them against experimental observations. It extends the framework to atomic, molecular, and organic chemistry.

The later chapters develop fluid dynamics of the brane, stochastic mechanics of the Markov trace, categorical information theory, quantum measurement as fibre-functor behaviour, and the q-geometric Langlands correspondence.
sec:models-qou-intro:
The QOU axioms admit realisations across diverse ground fields and geometric settings. This chapter separates the universal features forced by the axioms from the model-dependent features fixed by the ground ring and fibre geometry.

The Jones model arising from \mathbf{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) serves as the concrete anchor. Around it lies the wider landscape: archimedean realisations (Calabi–Yau, ALE spaces), p-adic quantum groups via Drinfeld's theory, finite-field models, and Witt-vector models. Each model instantiates the QOU axioms with different fibre geometry and ground rings. This illustrates the flexibility of the categorical framework while exposing the universal structural constraints. This landscape is surveyed through the physical interpretation of the q-weighted Yang–Mills–Levi functional and the main commutative diagram relating categorical and differential structures.
def:q-yang-mills-levi:
Definition q-Weighted curvature--Levi functional. Let (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) be an archimedean quantum observable universe with instanton connection A and aether parameter q. The q-weighted curvature–Levi functional is

  \mathfrak{S}_q[A, \varTheta]
  =  \int_M q(p)\lVert F_A^+|_H \rVert^2
        \varTheta \wedge (d\varTheta)^n,

where q(p) = 1 + \lvert\langle L_\varTheta, F_A^+\rangle\rvert(p).
prop:main-commutative-diagram:
Proposition Main Commutative Diagram. Let (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) be an archimedean quantum observable universe with instanton connection A and aether parameter q. Let \mathrm{EL} denote the Euler–Lagrange operator of the q-weighted Yang–Mills–Levi functional \mathfrak{S}_q. Let \nabla^A denote parallel transport along A. The upper-left object J^1\mathcal{S} is the space of 1-jets of sections of the state bundle \mathcal{S} (encoding the state and its first-order derivatives). The following diagram commutes:

\[
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=2.5em]
  J^1\mathcal{S}
    \ar[r, "{\mathrm{EL}[\mathfrak{S}_q]}"]
    \ar[d, "\text{jet evaluation}"']
  & \bigl\{ L_\varTheta : \mathrm{Ric}_{g_\varTheta} = T^{(q)} \bigr\}
    \ar[d, "{q = 1 + \lvert\langle L_\varTheta, F_A^+\rangle\rvert}"]
  \\
  \Gamma(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{lin}})
    \ar[r, "\nabla^A"']
  & \bigl\{ \psi : J\hbar_q\iota_{\xi_q}D_A\psi = \hat{H}_q\psi \bigr\}
\end{tikzcd}
\]

The reading of each edge — top row, columns, and bottom row — is given in the diagram interpretation.
rem:main-commutative-diagram-interpretat:
Remark Reading the main commutative diagram edge-by-edge. This square exhibits the Einstein-type field equation and the Schrödinger evolution as two faces of a single commuting diagram. The aether coupling q ties the gravitational and quantum dynamics together.

The top row sends a jet to the Einstein-type field equation via the Euler–Lagrange operator. The left column evaluates a jet at a fibre point to produce a linearised section. The right column implements the coupling through the aether field q. The bottom row applies the parallel-transport equation whose linearisation is the Schrödinger equation.
prf:main-commutative-diagram:
Proof Proof of Main Commutative Diagram. Commutativity is verified by tracing both paths around the diagram.

Top-right path (variational \to coupling). This path turns a jet into an aether parameter q and its Hamiltonian \hat{H}_q. Applying the Euler--Lagrange operator \mathrm{EL}[\mathfrak{S}_q] to a jet j^1_p \sigma yields the variational equation \mathrm{Ric}_{g_\varTheta} = T^{(q)}. Solving for L_\varTheta determines the Tanaka–Webster metric. This in turn fixes the aether field via the coupling q(p) = 1 + \lvert\langle L_\varTheta, F_A^+\rangle\rvert. This determines \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}, the q-Reeb field \xi_q, and the q-Hamiltonian \hat{H}_q = -\tfrac{1}{2}\hbar_q\Delta_q + V_q appearing in the transport equation.

Left-bottom path (evaluation \to transport). This path turns the same jet into a transported wavefunction \psi. The jet evaluation map j^1_p \sigma \mapsto \sigma(p) produces a section \psi \in \Gamma(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{lin}}) by linearising the fibre \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) at the chosen base-point. Parallel transport along A then imposes J\hbar_q\iota_{\xi_q} D_A\psi = \hat{H}_q\psi (Schrödinger equation).

Commutativity. Both paths share the same input (j^1_p \sigma) and output (a section \psi satisfying the transport equation at aether parameter q). The chain rule for the composite \mathfrak{S}_q[\nabla, L_\varTheta, \psi] factorises the variation into two coupled equations:

  1. \delta \mathfrak{S}_q / \delta L_\varTheta = 0 determines L_\varTheta (hence q and \hat{H}_q) along the top row.
  2. \delta \mathfrak{S}_q / \delta \psi = 0 yields D_\nabla\psi = 0 (variational equations, Item 3) along the bottom row.

The coupling q = 1 + \lvert\langle L_\varTheta, F_A^+\rangle\rvert ensures that the parameter q matches along both paths. The non-degeneracy of \int_A (Frobenius pairing) guarantees the solution sets agree. Solving for L_\varTheta first and substituting into the transport equation yields the same \psi as evaluating the jet and transporting along A.
sec:crossing-energy-levi-intro: Away from the symmetric point q = 1, the elementary crossing weight \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) and the square (q - 1)^2 combine into a strictly positive rational functional on (1, \infty) that vanishes on the 2-torsion locus \mu_2 = \{1, -1\}. Paired with the variation of the q-weighted curvature--Levi functional with respect to the Levi form on a CR manifold, this records the algebraic positivity and geometric back-reaction properties of the model prior to the symmetric-point degeneration.
prop:crossing-energy-gap:
Proposition Crossing-energy gap positivity and \mu_2-vanishing. For real q \neq 0, define the minimum crossing weight \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) and the crossing-energy gap functional

  \Delta_q := \mathfrak{E}_\times(q)\,(q - 1)^2 = \frac{(q^2 - 1)(q - 1)^2}{2q}.

Then:

  1. For every real q > 1, \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) > 0 and \Delta_q > 0.
  2. At the symmetric point q = 1, \Delta_1 = 0, and across \mathbb{R}^\times the factor q^2 - 1 vanishes precisely on the 2-torsion subgroup \mu_2 = \{1, -1\}.
  3. On (1, \infty), \Delta_q is monotonically increasing: 1 < q_1 \le q_2 implies \Delta_{q_1} \le \Delta_{q_2}.
prf:crossing-energy-gap: Proof Proof of crossing-energy gap positivity and monotonicity. For q \neq 0, clearing denominators gives \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) = (q^2 - 1)/(2q). When q > 1, both q^2 - 1 > 0 and 2q > 0, so \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) > 0, and (q - 1)^2 > 0, giving \Delta_q > 0. Direct substitution at q = 1 gives \Delta_1 = 0, while for q \in \mathbb{R}^\times the numerator (q - 1)^3(q + 1) vanishes if and only if q \in \{1, -1\} = \mu_2. Finally, for 1 < q_1 \le q_2, the map q \mapsto q - q^{-1} and the map q \mapsto (q - 1)^2 are both positive and non-decreasing, so their product \Delta_q satisfies \Delta_{q_1} \le \Delta_{q_2}. \square
